clauses.text: Never PR a feature branch straight into `main`.
Keep this file current in the same PR.
Never push directly to `main`.
add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry in the same change. A `dev → main` merge with no bump is a no-op release. -
A release is cut by a version bump, not by a merge.
never say a workflow works
clauses.rationale: Rungs 0-2 prove refs are real and the YAML is clean. Only a green CI run proves it works. Conflating the two is exactly the failure this skill was built against.

clauses.text: never\s+hand-write it
clauses.rationale: The brand lives in press/brand/tokens.json and nowhere else. Hand-writing a masthead recreates precisely the drift press exists to end — this brand was previously eight hand-ported copies across four repos with five names for the same orange.

clauses.text: never interpolate .github\.event\.. into a `run:` block
clauses.rationale: `${{ }}` is textual substitution performed before the shell sees the string, so an attacker-controlled PR title is source code, not an argument. This is the most common real vulnerability in real workflows.

clauses.text: secret\s+names only
clauses.rationale: Detection reads `gh secret list` to know what exists. A secret VALUE entering the process or the transcript would turn a convenience feature into a credential leak.

clauses.text: recommend against it\s\n?\suntil the check has gone green once
clauses.rationale: A required check that never passes blocks every future merge — a repo-wide outage produced by a helpful default. The check must be observed green before it gates anything.

clauses.text: staleness is invisible to every linter
clauses.rationale: A hand-written fixture pinning actions/checkout@v5 passed actionlint AND zizmor completely clean while two majors behind. Published research puts the typical workflow 7+ months behind. Existence is not currency, and only forge reports the difference.

clauses.text: One script call, not a pipeline.
Report in tables, with named columns.
Never claim a visual result without the artifact.
Never print file contents into the conversation.
Announce the skill once, at the start
Keep the machinery invisible.
Show, don't describe.
Say which rung you reached, and never claim more.
Never add a required status check without asking, and recommend against it until the check has gone green once.
fix what it finds, re-run.
Never silently overwrite an existing workflow.
Never emit an action ref you have not resolved.
Never interpolate `${{ github.event.* }}` into a `run:` block.

Run the commands the workflow will run — locally, now.
